case_name: Mungeshwar Prasad Chaurasia and Another v State of Bihar
respondent:
State of Bihar
Supreme Court of India

13 September 2001
Cr.A. No. 940 of 2001 (arising out of S.L.P. (Cri) No. 4277 of 2000), Dt. 13 September 2001.
The Order of the Court was as follows:
Leave granted.
1.  Three persons were convicted under Sections 304-B, 201 read with Sections 34 and 498-A of the Indian Penal Code. The present appellants were sentenced to RI for seven years each for the first count and RI for two years on the second count while no separate sentence was awarded for the third count. As for the remaining convicted person the sentence awarded on the first count was RI for nine years (Ram Pukar).
All the convicted persons appealed before the High Court and the conviction as well as sentence were confirmed. The present appellants are A1-Mungeshwar Prasad and A3-Devanti Devi. Their son Ram Pukar is the remaining convicted person who has not challenged the verdict of the High Court. So we are dealing with this appeal only in respec
facts: The present appellants were sentenced to RI for seven years each for the first count and RI for two years on the second count while no separate sentence was awarded for the third count.
Sudama Devi was married to the son of the appellants-Ram Pukar sometime during 1992. She died of unnatural circumstances on 24-1-95.
The convicted persons are alleged to have subjected her to harassments with the demand for dowry and after her death she was hurriedly cremated.
Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that A1-Mungeshwar Prasad and his wife A3-Devanti Devi are very old people having crossed 80 years of age even at the time of death of Sudama Devi.
petitioner_arguments: The plea made on that score was to have the sentence reduced.
Some of the witnesses said that soon after marriage these appellants asked for more dowry. But that demand was made at a time which was beyond the range of 'soon before death' of the deceased.
court_reasoning: The prosecution did not succeed in showing that the present appellants did anything for subjecting Sudama Devi to harassment with the demand for dowry 'soon before her death'.
All of them said in one accord that husband of Sudama Devi demanded dowry a few months prior to her death.

Of course some of the witnesses said that soon after marriage these appellants asked for more dowry. But that demand was made at a time which was beyond the range of 'soon before death' of the deceased.
